The scope looks good and it was easy to install. I have many scopes and if I have any problems w/it, just like all my reviews, I will come back here and adjust my ratings accordingly.

Just FYI, I installed this scope on my new Henry X Rifle 45-70 w/the Weaver 63B mount and a set of Vortex Pro-Series 1" low rings. If you mount this scope on this rifle w/the low mounts it will fit. If you were to get a 40mm or higher scope, the front housing would sit on or hit the rifle's rear sight. If you purchase a larger than 32mm scope, I would recommend buying the medium scope rings. I went w/the 2-7x32mm specifically so that I could use the low scope rings, as I didn't want to have to raise my cheek weld. It's my determination that a 2-7x32 scope will be sufficient for the yardages I will likely shoot a 45-70 at.
text_fidelity_b: Vortex Optics Crossfire II Second Focal Plane, 1-inch Tube Riflescopes

text_fidelity_a:
Snowshoes for Adult Unisex,Fully Adjustable Bindings, Lightweight Material, Hard Pack Grip Teeth,Outdoor Aluminum Alloy Material Really like these snowshoes. They are easy to adjust and stay on very well. The bag the shoes came in is first rate as are the poles. My only complaint is that the front binding only ratchets to a point then seem to hang up (it could be the strap end catching on the decking, or perhaps the hard boot material failing to flex)not a huge deal because it is snug enough. Also the pole carrying bag is separate from the shoe bag which means I got to remember to grab both. All in all a nice inexpensive snowshoe. Great for beginners or someone just needing a cheaper option.
12/29/11 UPDATE_ Got to try these out for the first time (not real deep snow- but enough to give them a trial run) These shoes are really nice. I tromped around for about 30 mins and had very few problems (main problem was some ice build up on my heel as I crossed a wet area and the water froze on my boot heel- not a big deal as it can happen with any snowshoe). The bindings did hold well and did not loosen at all. One shoe did seem to be toeing in a bit but that was probably an adjustment issue (it was also a new pair of boots I was trying out.) I'm gonna hopefully get out in some deeper snow next week (yea Lake Effect!)
1/15/12 UPDATE2- Finally got some REAL snow (18+ inches!) and tried these out at my hilly property in the deep woods. AMAZING how well they worked. It was pretty cold (hovering around 16° F in the sun) and the woods were untouched by anything but a few deer and turkeys. These shoes performed great. They never slipped and I did not have to adjust the bindings at all. They do seem to make a bit of noise as far as the bindings creaking (at these temps not to surprising), but nothing broke or loosened. Walked for a little over an hour; over logs, thru brush, uphill, downhill, level, tight twisty area, open fields, deep drifts, and even a snowmobile trail (that crosses the front of our property). These preformed as good as any other shoe. A bonus is I found I really liked the poles- so much so that I gave one to my wife and she really liked using it too. All in all a great purchase- These honestly hover on a 5 star rating- I did have to take away for the pole bag not being attached some way- also the poles are nearly impossible to closeup once they get cold (I think a bit of frost gets into the loosening cam and freezes the pole in place as once they warmed up there were no problems) also there is no place to store the rubber protection cap from the pole. The one show still seemed to toe in a bit- but I only notice it in very shallow snow (less than 6 inches) and the toe binding still only rachets to a certain point and then slips (still not an issue as it is snug enough). Oh and of course the noise factor (not real bad but your not gonna sneak up on anything with these on)
text_fidelity_b: Snowshoes for Adult Unisex,Fully Adjustable Bindings, Lightweight Material, Hard Pack Grip Teeth,Outdoor Aluminum Alloy Material

The skull cap was comfy to put on and warms up well to keep my head warm and that's what I really want and the reason I gave it four stars.

I never had heard of, or played, cornhole until it was introduced to me at a social gathering relatively recently. I have wanted my own set for taking to family functions and picnics with friends, and this set is well suited for these situations.

I will start with this: I received the tailgate version which is a little smaller than the regulation size set. The difference is that the boards are a foot shorter. Second, because it is smaller it is more compact and can be stored (and transported) more easily too.

This set instead has an aluminum frame and lightweight boards so the weight is substantially reduced. The legs fold under, allowing the set to lay flat. This makes it a lot easier to pack the set for travel and to store it away when not in use. An important detail – when the legs are down they lock in place with a metal bracket so the board will not collapse.

The set comes with 8 bean bags, 4 blue and 4 red. These are regulation size and are interchangeable with other sets.

So far my family is very pleased with this set. It is made very well, it is compact and portable, and because this set (in my case) is the tailgate version it is lighter and easier to store when not in use. This is an easy product to recommend.

A friend has one. So this came to mind. I just rest them on each shoulder (I have broad shoulders).

Of the many I researched online, this fit the bill best for higher weight capacity (15lbs total with the 2 on), comfort, looks, price, and staying put on my shoulders.

Fabric is soft but pretty durable, although for true ankle wearing walking I agree with reviews, the fabric would wear down with the heavier weighted ones just due to the fact that a required soft fabric (so not nylon) that’s comfortable on skin must break down with shear, and the heavier the weight the more inherent shear (friction) there’ll be. But, stick to a classic lower weight and that’s not a big issue with these. Go with another that’s more durable and it’ll scratch your skin more. It’s a catch 22.

Anyway, these are great, but particularly for women for whom future osteoporosis could be a thing if you wear them slung over your shoulders.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Renn 50 Women's Backpacking Backpack, Challenger Blue We’ve always had good experience with Osprey for water packs and day packs. This is our first hiking pack, and it shows the same degree of quality and design. Short version is this is an excellent mid-size pack, well made, well constructed, and comfortable. Though of course that last is highly individual—try it on (with weight and walking some distance instead of around your living room) before taking it out on that four-night overnighter!

Pros:
Torso adjustment: No excuse nowadays to buy a pack without a good torso adjuster (if you’re still using an ancient pack without an easily -adjustable torso length, it’s way past time to upgrade!). This one has a good range and is easy to use It’s well ventilated off the back (tension keeps it off your back for more air flow)

Lightweight: certainly way lighter than your 15-year-old pack I’d guess and ligheter than most modern ones as well.

Straps: again, something of personal preference. But I’d say these are nicely adjustable, have the right amount of padding and width. Some can be too narrow, too wide, over or under-padded. The Osprey is in the sweet spot.

Hipbelt: Like above—good thickness, comfortable. Zippered pockets always a nice touch for a Cliff bar or map etc. These ones are a noticeably bigger than the ones on our old packs, which is a nice change.

Organization: Pretty traditional/basic. This isn’t the pack with lots of bells and whistles and mini-pockets etc. But it’s effective, easy to use.

Hydration sleeve: fits a good size reservoir (up to 3 L)

Rain cover: you’ll need someone to get it out for you or put your pack down, but again, it’s effective and nice to have

Side pockets: I’m not a fan of the diagonal pockets—I prefer the vertical ones even if it’s a little harder to get your stuff out because they’re more likely to stay in the pocket when you lean/bend. These are OK, and certainly lots of packs have these diagonal ones; I just like the older version.

Cons
No outer mesh pocket for easy to grab/stash items, particularly a rain coat.

On the smaller size, though not really a con since you buy the pack that best fits you and best meets your needs (or multiple packs for multiple needs—i.e. a 2-nighter vs. a 5-nighter or a summer hike versus a winter hike with bulkier clothes, sleeping bags, etc)

Good price for such a good pack
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Renn 50 Women's Backpacking Backpack, Challenger Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Prorack Kayak Carrier My only previous experience carrying kayaks has been tying them to the top of a rental car with old patch cords through the windows. So my comments here might not be wise, but hopefully a fresh perspective.

First thing I noticed is that you have to have the cross bars installed on your roof rack, not just the bars that run perpendicular to your windshield.

I really like the idea and design on the four "pads" that you lock down, they flex in (or out) to conform somewhat to the bottom of your vessel. They give you confidence that the pressure you apply is working with you and not against you (not that you're applying too much).

They lock on fairly easily with a simple bolt and sort of a wing-nut type add-on. This could be slightly better. You have to pull that wing-nut add-on back to encase the head of the bolt, which is intuitive and not difficult, but the system reminds me of a tool for cutting lock holes in doors that I broke the first day. An all metal specialty-bolt would inspire much more confidence.

The straps they give you are just okay. They work, but they're not the heavy duty ratcheting straps you might be imagining. Similarly the ropes and hooks they give you to tie down the front and the back are less impressive than some specialty-cut bungee cords with rubber-covered hooks on one end and quick attachment mechanism on the other that you might wish for.

I don't have a high opinion of the general public, and thus I remove all such equipment from my car, even when it is possible to lock it in place. Locks are always appreciated, though, although half the time they are just "best effort" on these types of devices anyway. Even so, they're fairly quick to remove and replace, especially if you can mark or remember the exact placement.

In summary, this is a good (and apparently unique, from reading other reviews) idea, and the bulk of the product seems to be of high quality. A few bucks extra spent on higher quality accessories would kick this up to a premium product.
text_fidelity_b: Prorack Kayak Carrier

Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm) This yoga mat has a lovely color and attractive patterns embossed in its textured surface. It is well made of high-quality, sustainable, latex-free rubber, and the ribbed bottom works well for preventing slippage on a smooth surface.

This mat out-gassed a slight chemical smell for a few days but it did eventually wear off.

The manufacturer claims this mat is "thick." It seems to me to be about the same thickness, or at best a tiny bit thicker, than the standard rubber mats provided at my gym. For what it is worth, I have this to say about all such mats: If your body doesn't come with it's own built-in "padding," it is a bruising experience to do yoga or calisthenic exercises on a hard floor while sitting or lying on this or any other thin, rubber mat. For that reason, there aren't any yoga mats of this type on the market, including this one, that seem "thick" to me personally. However, since that is a typical design feature among all rubber yoga mats, I am not grading down this mat for not being what I truly consider thick--a depth of three inches. That is the thickness of a different type of yoga mat, a [[ASIN:B003VQNM2I futon mat]], which I also own. The advantage of this mat over a futon mat is that it weighs 5 pounds vs 19 pounds for the futon mat, making it much more portable. It is also substantially easier to keep clean.

Speaking of cleaning this mat, it is not necessary to pay a lot of money for special yoga-mat cleaning solutions when a mat is made of rubber, as this one is. You can make your own quite inexpensively. Here are some examples:

1. Dilute white vinegar in a ratio of 1:16 (1 tablespoon per cup). Vinegar is a natural disinfectant. To increase disinfectant properties, you can add a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice or a few drops of any of the following essential oils which each have disinfectant properties: tea tree, eucalyptus, peppermint, lavender, oregano, lemon, and clove.

2. Dilute a biodegradeable liquid soap, such as [[ASIN:B00016QTYO Sal Suds]], in the same proportion as the white vinegar, 1:16.

3. You can add 1 tablespoon liquid soap to each cup of white-vinegar mixture to maximize cleaning effectiveness.

Instructions for use of cleaning solutions:

1. Put the cleaning solution of your choice in a spray bottle and shake well.

2. Spray the mat and use a clean rag or paper towel to scrub the mat.

3. If you use a soap mixture, you may want to go back over the mat with a clean, damp rag or damp paper towel in order to remove the soap residue. This is not necessary when you use a vinegar mixture.

Note that rubber is not harmed by water. This means that, if you wanted to, you could hose it off on your patio during warm-weather seasons and drape it over a patio chair or the rail of a deck or porch to dry.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz I simply LOVE my insulated Eddy Cambelbak bottle!
I didn't have a clue what they were all about, nor how a bite valve worked, but I needed a water bottle and started reading up about them. I am converted!
This bottle is very well constructed, and although tall, it doesn't take up much space on a desk or side table, and it holds a good 0.6L volume of lovely iced water.....and it doesn't "sweat"! Fantastic!
It keeps my water nice and cool for ages, and it is so convenient that I find myself drinking a lot more water that before, which is a good thing.

For anyone else that doesn't know what bite valve is (can I be the only one??!) - the "spout" of this bottle is made of a firm silicon rubber and it has a closed hole that attaches down to the bottle's straw. When you bite the end of this spout or valve, it squeezes the hole open and you just suck up the water like drinking from a straw. The second you take pressure off and stop biting down, the hole closes shut again and - voila! - A leak proof bottle! It is a fantastic design - I love it! (see pic)

The valve part can be in an angled or upright position, so you don't have to tip the bottle sideways to get the water to flow, and it also pushes right back to a "closed" and flat position which is great if you have it in a backpack, beach bag etc. It is just a really innovative design and it really works so well!!
I highly recommend this bottle to anyone who wants a fantastic, no sweat, leak-proof, easy to use drinking bottle - 10/10 !
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak eddy Insulated Water Bottle, 20oz

Yoga Mat - With Carry Strap -Great Pilates And Exercise Mat With Carry Sling -Save on Yoga Mat Bag-Best Classic Yoga Mat - 1/8" (3mm) Thick -Great Workout Mats For Women Kids And Men- Eco Friendly- Best Non-Slip Yoga Mat for Carpet, Home And Travel-On Sale-100% Money Back GUARANTEED! (Purple) NOTE: I received a free sample of this yoga mat for review purposes.

I have been practicing yoga for almost 15 years, and during that time, I have owned approximately ten different mats. My favorite is the one that I currently use both at home and for my classes, which is my [[ASIN:B00AB3LLVS Manduka eKO Lite Yoga Mat]]--I prefer its relatively thin profile, and it is one of the few mats that I have tried that is completely non-slip. However, my very first mat--an inexpensive version purchased at a discount clothing store--has a nice pebbled texture that has continued to perform quite well. (I keep that one at work.)

Yet, I'm always interested in trying new mats, as I donate them to others if I can't use them myself. This mat is an attractive purple color, and it comes with a convenient slip-on carry strap, something that most of my other mats don't have (I generally use a mat bag for class). What is most remarkable about this mat, however, is that is absolutely the LIGHTEST mat I have ever owned/used--to the point of feeling quite flimsy. Although it is the exactly same width as my Manduka Lite (3mm), the material of this mat has absolutely no substance to it, lacking the weightiness of my Manduka mat. Still, a lightweight mat is not necessarily a bad thing, as it can be convenient for travel. And one nice thing about this mat is that it is actually thin enough that it can be folded (again, it is thinner than a Gaiam mat I have which is DESIGNED to be folded), so that could come in handy for those wanting to stash a mat in their suitcase.

With respect to performance, however, I found this mat to be disappointing. Although this mat felt fairly secure for standing postures, no matter what I tried, my hands slipped on the mat in downward facing dog. I certainly would NOT feel secure attempting arm balances on this mat! Furthermore, although the mat is described as "eco-friendly," the only evidence of this appears to be that it uses "Phthalate-free inks"--no other information is provided about whether the mat's materials are from natural sources, such as rubber or bamboo.

In the end, I would recommend this mat ONLY if you are looking for a yoga mat that is super-lightweight and can fold into a suitcase. Otherwise, there are better choices available, and you can likely find better options at your local big box store.

text_fidelity_a:
LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out I already had a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell that I liked a lot (though it's not perfect), but I wanted another adjustable kettlebell with lower weights for certain types of work. After four months of regular use, it's still in good shape and I'm glad I bought it.

Changing the plates is not as fast as on the Bowflex model, but it's easy, although the sliding tab sticks now and then. Still, it's fast enough for me to continue through a circuit without losing momentum, and that's what's important to me.

All the plates weight 2.5 lbs, and you can remove them however you like. That is, you don't have to take them from the top or the bottom. You will have to slot them back into the same place they came from, however, because they all curve in a certain way to give the kettlebell it's shape. The reviewer who mentioned sharp edges makes a good point, one worth considering for different exercises. For example, for swings it makes no difference to me where I pull the plates from, but if I'm doing shoulder presses, I pull them from the bottom or else I'll get my forearm unpleasantly poked and scraped as I use it. For a bottoms up carry, I find keeping the plates loaded at the top makes the weight more stable as I walk.

The plates make a slight rattle when swung -- that doesn't bother me, but it's something to keep in mind if working out within earshot of someone who might be disturbed by the noise. The plates do feel secure within the bell, but I still make it a habit to swing it so that the plates would fly away from me rather than at me if they came loose, and I swing them toward a wall or some other area where the plate wouldn't damage anyone. All that said, I'm sure I'm being overly cautious.

One thing I really like about this is the overall shape and footprint as compared to the Bowflex adjustable kettlebell. This one is a standard kettlebell size -- that makes it easier for me to handle, especially when it's in close to my body. The Bowflex is much larger, and that makes certain moves really awkward. It's not fair to compare these, though, given that they have very different weight ranges, but it's something I noticed. In those few places where the weights overlap, I almost always reach for this kettlebell over the Bowflex.

When buying exercise equipment, I'd much rather go to a shop where I can try it out in person and comparison shop. The pandemic made that impossible, so I crossed my fingers and hoped for the best. And it worked out. Even with its flaws, I've definitely gotten my money's worth for this.
text_fidelity_b: LUBAN 35 LB Adjustable Dumbbell and Kettlebell for Men and Women, Perfect for Home, Office, Gym Work Out

5U+ Stainless Steel Water Bottle - Durable Portable Water Bottle 20 Oz Leakproof Thermos Water Jug Large Capacity Water Bottle Reusable Suitable For Hiking Fitness(Blue) PROS

1. It has an attractive, sleek, modern design. I got the black color, and it is a lovely, sharp, deep black.
2. A sturdy loop is firmly attached to the cap. It can be hooked onto a backpack using a carabiner or you could thread a belt through it.
3. The inside of this water bottle is stainless steel although, inevitably, the cap is made of plastic.
4. This water bottle can also serve as a thermos, which can keep hot drinks hot and cold drinks cold for about six hours.
5. The cap seals firmly to prevent leaking. It has a pop top for drinking without removing the cap. Press down on the top of the cap to open it and allow water to flow through, then press down again on the top to close it.
6. The matte finish of the bottle is slip proof, both on the sides and bottom.
7. The shape of this bottle is slender enough to easily fit in a cup holder in a car, on a bike, or on the side of a backpack.

CONS

1. There is a big downside of the fancy, pop-top of this cap. The part of the cap that liquid flows through is inaccessible to be cleaned with even the thinnest of straw brushes. This means that, in order to avoid buildup of mold within the cap from the residue of saliva and whatever liquids besides water you might put into this container, it is important that, after every use, you soak the cap in warm, soapy water for at least a few minutes, rinse it really well, and let it drain upside-down on a dish rack with plenty of ventilation so that any remaining water inside the cap can fully evaporate. Otherwise, within short order, you will be drinking slimy mold along with whatever liquids you put in this thermos. Note that, putting this cap in the dishwasher is not going to solve this problem. All it is likely to do is insure the cap is full of water that still needs to be drained out fully. And it possible that the heat of the dishwasher might damage the plastic of this cap, because the manufacturer does not state that this water bottle is dishwasher safe.

Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm) i received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased review. I was not influenced by anyone in any way.

Yoga balls are a great exercise item. I have a hard time doing sit ups and using the Yoga Ball, helps with doing them much easier. I used to be able to do pushups, putting my feet on the yoga ball and hands on the floor and do my pushups, but well yeah, that was a while back. So can not do that now. These really help with exercising the abs, waist, back, arms, hips, leg, gluts and other muscles. They are great for sitting at your desk. It forces proper spine alignment. Another great thing about using this alternative to a chair, is that you can do stretches or mini-workouts whenever you want, without getting up.

Your body primarily uses your core (abdominal) muscles to help compensate for changes in balance. So, you are essentially getting a low-key abdominal workout. Doesn't sound like much huh? But just consider the amount of time you spend on your computer at the office, or at home. Those hours can build up, and result in a strengthening of ab muscles. Not having a chair back to slouch into or armrests to lean on, you're almost forced to keep your back straight, which can encourage better posture. So get on that Yoga Ball and get movin! I know I am.

Besides developing good overall muscle tone for your entire body, the yoga ball provides many other benefits like rehabilitating back, hip, and knee injuries and getting a great workout to improve core stability, posture, and muscle balance. By using a low-impact workout, you will also improve your flexibility and your cardiovascular system.
PROS:
helps improve your balance - as we get older especially, we lose balance and mobility.
improves your circulation
you will feel more energetic
it's made with environmental friendly, non-toxic material.

CONS:
not really anything bad to say about a yoga ball. It's "all" good

OVERALL: This Yoga Ball is a quality product. Keeps the air really good.
text_fidelity_b: Housmile Exercise Stability Yoga Ball, Perfect Ball Chair for Home or Office (Purple 55cm)

text_fidelity_a:
Kamagon Exercise Ball, Blue, 9-Inch with workout DVD This Kamagon ball gives me a fun and somewhat strenuous workout.

The ball is the perfect size and weight for me to handle.

It's the perfect weight because I adjusted it to the 4 pound level (by filling it with water) recommended for beginners. The side of the ball is clearly marked with weight line guides that indicate 4 through 12 pounds.

Kamagon is approximately the size of a basketball. The easy-grip handles on each side make it bigger. The handles are easy to grab during the exercises. This is important because, while the water inside the ball creates an instability that promotes a full core workout, the water seems to be sloshing in one direction while the ball is going in the other direction. No problem though with the big handles. What is interesting about this "destabilized weight" is that my awareness seems to be amplified during the workout. On the back of the Owner's Manual it says, "works the muscles while simultaneously training your nervous system." Yes, I can feel my brain working as my muscles and brain adjust to the movement of the water inside of the ball.

The DVD has two vigorous workouts. The Owner's Manual has workouts with clear black and white photos. There is also plenty of online support via the Kamagon website, facebook, and YouTube. There is a "Kamagon Workout Guide" included. You can eventually work up to five days a week with two days set aside for rest.

Be sure to read and follow the Owner's Manual before starting.

This ball had a strong odor when it first arrived -- I could smell it from across the room. I placed it outside overnight and now I can barely detect any smell at all.

I love this workout method that promotes balance, strength, aerobic endurance and neuromuscular coordination.
text_fidelity_b: Kamagon Exercise Ball, Blue, 9-Inch with workout DVD

More about that below. The main issue I have and why I subtracted a star is it's a little on the narrow side. Otherwise, it's perfect. And for me that includes the relative thinness because I tested it outside on my lawn and it was actually comfortable. Or as comfortable as it can be since laying on it is akin to walking a tightrope because of its narrowness.

When I claim it's cleverly designed I am not exaggerating. It self inflates by opening a valve. For me between the material and the inflation it was sufficiently thick to be comfortable on my lawn. Obviously it will require relatively level and soft (or at least rock free) ground. I closed the valve after it inflated and when I was ready to roll it up all I had to do was open the valve and tightly roll it.

The rolling up part was where I expected a struggle, but that was smooth. It does not roll back up as tightly as it's rolled when you first receive it, but there is still ample room to place it in the included carrying bag.

If I have one recommendation for improvement (aside from making it wider) it would be to use velro straps attached to the air pad instead of the elastic 'garters' that come with it. The 'garters' work fine, but can be easily misplaced. Otherwise, for me this is perfect.

text_fidelity_a:
Axiom Streamliner Road DLX Racks I am pleased with the rack. However, it did not come with any instructions. I was able to figure it out anyway. You have to take off your rear brake and mount the bracket on the brake bolt between the brake and the frame. You put your wheel skewer through the holes on the bottom. Note that this makes it annoying to remove the rear wheel.

As another reviewer noted, the bracket needs to be bent in order to fit. This is unavoidable because different bicycles have different frame geometry. It is easy to bend with pliers and I had it bent correctly in about 2 minutes.

Note also that it is a narrow rack and is meant for mounting bags or baskets on the sides. Mounting to the top is iffy. (I mounted a basket to the top anyway, using enough zip ties to make sure it won't move).

This rack is much more securely mounted than my old one, which was mounted with p-clips. It is also much lower and closer to the wheel which helps keep the weight down low so it doesn't affect handling as much.

If you have a road bike, you can definitely use this rack to increase your cargo capacity. I was looking for something like this for a while and I'm glad someone makes it.
text_fidelity_b: Axiom Streamliner Road DLX Racks

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Kids Horseshoes Set - Soft Indoor + Outdoor Horseshoes Game Set for Kids - (4) Plastic Horseshoes, (2) Ground Stakes + (2) Plastic Indoor Stakes Included - Perfect Game for Kids This set comes with 2 blue rubber horseshoes, 2 green rubber horseshoes, 2 plastic ground stakes which can be pressed into soft soil (do not use a hammer!) and 2 free standing targets made up of a 1' wide rubber circle base, a weighted plastic stake, and a stake support base. The horseshoes are large (6.5" x 7.5")--much larger than a real horseshoe. You hold them by the top of the U and toss them at the stake. The instructions say that the stakes should be set up 10-15 feet from each other, with one team throwing from one side and the other team throwing from the other side. They suggest 4 people playing, but it works for 1-4 players. You score points if the horseshoe lands with the post inside the U (3 points) or the horseshoe touching the post (2 points) or a certain distance from the stake (1 point).

I initially used the 14" ground stakes pushed halfway into soft soil, and the stakes held well against horseshoes hitting them. The 6" free-standing stake is shorter, so a throw that might catch the ground stake and make a score might fly over the free-standing stake. I was surprised, but the free-standing stakes also took hits without falling over--probably because they're weighted and the wide circle base pulls them back down when hit. Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway This is a great way to store 12 sets of polyhedral dice for D&D and similar games. I'm not sure if you strictly-speaking need waterproof storage for that, but while the O-ring may be overkill, the locking clasps and overall durability are a cut above what you usually find on parts organizers. This is never, ever going to come open unexpectedly and spill its precious contents all over the place!

With the dividers installed as shown in my photo, 8 areas hold a set of 7 polyhedral dice perfectly. Five of those will also hold a set of 12 six-sided dice. The four larger areas hold somewhat more; I have 10 d20's in one of them comfortably.

The downside of this approach is that you're certainly not going to sneak up on anyone while carrying one of these full of plastic/resin dice. And if you're into metal dice, or the sort of gemstone dice where each of them costs more than this whole container, then this probably isn't how you want to store them. (But you could probably pad them properly with a bit more work.)

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

If you are the sort of person who needs to compactly and securely transport a lot of dice, this is the best way I've found to do it.
text_fidelity_b: Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway

Coleman SupportRest Double-High Air Mattress for Indoor or Outdoor Use, Easily Inflatable Airbed with Plush Top & Carry Bag, Queen & Twin Options Available My wife and I recently got talked into a camping weekend, and as neither of us has camped in decades, we wanted to do so in a bit of luxury. I'm a rather large dude, and I've laid on enough beds that lost all of their air to know I wanted a good bed, and this is it!

The first night I mistakenly suggested filling it extra firm (we're both side sleepers fond of softer beds) thinking that it would inevitably lose air. It didn't :-( It was rock hard, like we inflated it. It didn't lose a single bit of air. The second night we took that into account and let a bit out, and it was much much more comfortable!

Inflating went easy with a Coleman AC air pump, and deflating went easy enough with some body weight and rolling. It was a bit tough to roll it nice and neat, but we got it rather compact again once we tried a bit harder at home.

My only complaint, and it's minor, the weird flocked side grabs dirt and cannot really be cleaned. We use sleeping bags and a sheet on it, so it's no biggie, but once a tiny bit of mud finds this, not even a clorox wipe will help.

That aside, this is an air mattress that can hold some serious weight and not lose any air. That's amazing given some nightmare experiences that I've had.

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack I'll try to get to the details not already mentioned multiple times:

FOLDED DIMENSIONS: 38"H x 15.5"D x 10"W when completely folded with the hitch bar removed. I was really pleased to see what a small footprint this takes up when not attached to the car. Folding takes about 40 seconds, and removing the hitch bar - if desired - takes another 60 or so and requires an allen wrench. I made a partially-sided box out of scrap wood to hold and protect this nicely behind the car in the garage when not in use.

When folded, the center bar and two side bars come to within about 1/8" of each other without touching - very nicely designed.

TIGHTENING MECHANISMS: I was delighted to see that the mechanisms to hand tighten the wheel holders are the high quality, non-abrasive clamping type, rather than the screw-down-a-machine-screw type that flakes paint and distorts metal over time.

CONSTRUCTION: All immovable joints are welded, the rubber straps on the wheel holders are very thick, and the ratcheting clamps are fantastic. The anti-wobble hitch pin works, but you'll need to carry your 19mm socket/wrench if you want to remove this at your cycling site (but it's quick and easy to fold and throw in the trunk).

LOCKING: It's been mentioned before over several reviews, but to consolidate points: One small lock will fit through the hitch pin nicely, but you need larger locks to keep the center arms from being removable. One reviewer enlarged his with a drill to make his next size larger lock fit, but I won't do the same to mine for fear of removing the finish, possibly making a weak point for rust to form. Locking the arms with the correct size lock is a great feature and a great selling point (actually, that was what finally got me to pick this one over the similar model by Hollywood Racks), but it would have been absolutely fantastic if the hitch pin and arm clamps took the same size lock so you could get a matching set that uses one key. Alternatively, I would have gladly paid a couple bucks more to have appropriate locks included.

Absolutely recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XTC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack

text_fidelity_a:
NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly I'm an Eagle Scout. We go Jeeping a lot. As an adult, we take our kids camping a LOT.

We've had this tent for 2 1/2 years and taken it camping probably 15-20 times. It's been all over the desert of NM, the mountains of Colorado, and the red rocks of Utah.

This tent is AWESOME.

PROS:
- Dome design doesn't require stakes in the ground - we have a lot of rocks up in the mountains.
- Dome design is super simple and quick to put up - usually about 2 minutes for us if we're taking our time.
- Walled sides - with the tub shape, water never gets in.
- It's HUGE. We usually put a full size air mattress AND two twin size mattresses in it PLUS there's about enough room for another twin mattress as well. We could probably fit two queen mattresses in there.
- It's TALL - my wife and I are both 6ft tall and can stand up in the middle very easily, not the "standing up but hunched over kind of" actually standing upright.
- The BAG IS AWESOME - hate trying to get a tent back into it's bag? This is the tent for you! Fold it into quarters, roll it up around the poles, throw it in, and because the bag is a little bigger than you need, it fits easily. (No, it's not loose and baggy, just right). We've had nights of "quick, just shove it in the bag" and it fits fine that way too. Easy to put away.
- HUGE POLES - you won't believe it till you see it, these poles are about as big around as a finger, not the little wimpy poles.
- BIG VENTS AND GIANT RAIN FLY - The vents on the sides are basically everything from the tub up to the top, so lots of ventilation. The Rain fly easily covers the mesh though and we've never had rain get in at all.
- No stakes necessary - we never use stakes, and the fly doesn't go anywhere and the tent stays put. We've shoved gear in the corners or occasionally a big rock, and done really well with this.

CONS:
- We had one of the bungee strings break in the poles, but that's to be expected after some use. It was easy enough to fix. The overall design is sturdy enough we used it a few times with no bungee at all and it was ok.
- Cooler weather - it has huge vents on the sides under the fly, so heat gets out when it's cold. But, we've also shoved a blanket or one of those two person hammocks between the tent and the fly and that helps keep the heat in a little better. Let's just say, it's probably not any colder than most other tents like this.
- Size. It is big, and if you need space to sprawl it's there. But if it's a cramped area because of trees, it is pretty big. If you're out west, and there's lots of room, this is a great tent.

CONCLUSION:
I've owned a 6-8 different tents, most of them dome tents, and this one is the toughest built, the most well-thought out, and the easiest to work with. I'd definitely buy this tent again.

(and if you have the space in your vehicle, throw some of those foam puzzle floor pieces in the tent and it makes it really, really posh)

(No, I didn't get this tent for free or anything, bought it outright).
text_fidelity_b: NTK Cherokee GT 8 to 9 Person 10 by 12 Foot Outdoor Dome Family Camping Tent 100% Waterproof 2500mm, Easy Assembly, Durable Fabric Full Coverage Rainfly

Thing is I tried this next to my other bottles and this was by far the worst at keeping drinks cold. Ice melted in 3 hours or less every time I tried, that’s with half a tray of ice cubs + refrigerated water. All others kept the ice solid for at least 6+ hours.

The style of the bottle is a 5. But if it cannot keep ice from melting and drinks cold as long as my other bottles and tumblers? It’s useless to me. May be good for at home when you can constantly refresh ice and drinks. When traveling? It’s not going to work for me and that’s the main reason I got it. I feel very disappointed especially when they send me emails bragging about how they keep drinks colder way longer than others claim to. They don’t they’re the opposite or what they claim to be.

I tried to review it on their site, but couldn’t get it approved so the product has 5 stars there but I wouldn’t trust that star count.

*update* got a different brand and decided to compare how fast they lose their ability to stay cool. This bottle went from 35 degree water to 66.3 in 3.5 hours. While the other bottle took over 24 hours to get that warm.

Viper Dead-On Tournament Bristle Steel Tip Dartboard Set with Staple-Free Bullseye, Metal Triangular Spider Wire for Reduced Bounce Outs and Increased Scoring; High-Grade Self-Healing Sisal Board The dead-on viper sisal fiber dartboard is a classic dartboard that you will likely see in your local bar or pub. The spider, or the metal that separates the segments (numbers and colors), is angled on each side. Therefore, if a dart barely hits the side of the spider then it will be directed to hit the sisal fibers. The angled spider helps reduce the number of bounce backs. However, you should notice that the spider has "staples" that go over the metal bar on both sides. If you do not like this aspect of the dartboard then you can spend an extra $10-$15 bucks and upgrade to the viper spider dartboard. Either board is a great addition to your home game room or man (or woman) cave. Great board. Made in Taiwan.

TINEMET Weighted Jump Rope - (1LB) Solid PVC for Crossfit and Boxing - Heavy Jump Rope for Fitness Workouts Endurance and Strength Training Working out can involve many different types of equipment. I tend to prefer the workouts that need as little equipment as possible and jumping rope is a good way to workout using something that is simple and can be taken and used most anywhere. A good choice for your next jump rope workout is TINEMET Weighted Jump Rope.

Weighing more than the typical jump rope, this heavier rope is not really a rope at all, and that is good because it can’t get tangled like an actual rope. It’s also easier to jump over than a traditional jump rope so you are less likely to trip while you use it. The cable glides across the floor with ease, in contrast to an actual rope which can sometimes cause friction when it touches the floor.

There is more weight with this jump rope and you will notice it in the handles, which include a weight in each. If you like, you can unscrew the ends of the handles and remove the weights. I think it’s best to leave them in place, since the added weight can improve a workout. Besides, they are quite light and are certainly not heavy enough to make jumping rope uncomfortable. Another cool feature is that you can pull the rope through the handles and trim it down to size. This is great because it means that shorter individuals can adjust it to fit their needs.

Jumping rope is a good activity to add to any workout. This TINEMET Weighted Jump Rope is a handy addition to your exercise needs. It glides and turns easily and the adjustable feature makes it usable by just about anyone. It’s a good gift idea for the exercise fans among your family and friends.
text_fidelity_b: TINEMET Weighted Jump Rope - (1LB) Solid PVC for Crossfit and Boxing - Heavy Jump Rope for Fitness Workouts Endurance and Strength Training

Etekcity Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Accessories Gear Tent Lights, Lanterns Battery Powered LED for Power Outages, Survival Kits, Operated Lamp, 4 Pack This small lantern is a little less than 5 1/2" tall and about 3 1/2" in diameter. If you need smaller, then you need a flashlight! As for light, it has plenty! I have 2 LED lanterns 10" tall by 5" dia. and they put out half as much light as these smaller ones. My bigger ones are not efficient enough to read by, these are. I need these strictly for outages, which we seem to have a lot of, and I appreciate the area coverage of these. No, it will not make it easy to read a few feet away from them, no lantern does that, but it will make it easy to see and navigate in a 15' x 15' room.
They are adjustable in only one way, and that is how much you open them. (At just high enough to turn them on, they make great guiding lights for a footpath or a cluttered area.) All the bulbs are on no matter how close to closed it is, so there is no power saving advantage to having it lowered. 12 Hours of emergency or evening lighting outside, is a lot of hours! It will more than stand up to all emergency needs except getting lost in a cave! LOL If it only had 3-4 hours of good light, I would not be happy with this, my first thought is always 'how to extend the emergency light time' and 'is it adjustable'. Well, you can't, and its not....Because of that this would not be an economic idea for an extended camping trip. But this is not being touted as a night after night lighting fix, as an emergency light, I don't need to worry about that.
I joined Etekcity's review program, because I have purchased several of their products and haven't found one I didn't appreciate a lot! As such I don't feel bad about getting one of their products at a reduced price or free for reviewing them. I take my time, and look at all the negative reviews and see if any apply to the product i received. So far.... yes it is pretty light, but no it would not blow away in less that 50mph winds. And i don't think you would be outside enjoying an evening in that kind of wind anyway. It has the hard anodized look and feeling of a well coated flashlight. The handles are wide enough to be easy to carry and a bungee cord or rope will attach them to the side of any tree or post, or you can hang them from a limb or tent pole. Heavy enough not to tip over, and good quality plastic instead of glass or cheep plastic that cracks. I don't see anything cheap or flimsy feeling about them at all!
Don't know what else to say about these, except my other two larger ones are going out into storage and I will be getting 2 more of these to store inside for emergencies. I highly recommend them!
PS: If you DO get a lemon, for Pete's sake tell them! They are very quick and easy to talk to. There is a card in the box with a toll free number, their e-mail address and their website on it (etekcity.com).... all for customer support.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Accessories Gear Tent Lights, Lanterns Battery Powered LED for Power Outages, Survival Kits, Operated Lamp, 4 Pack

Vittoria Competition Latex Tube - Performance Bike Tire Tube - Lightweight Bicycle Inner Tubes for Racing Yes, they'll lose air. I toured with these and found myself down 20 psi every morning of the tour. I'd pump them up to 100 psi and be down to 80 again by the next morning. With a good pump, this is not a big deal. Just plan on pumping them up every day that you ride. I don't ride often enough for that to be an ordeal, and even if I rode everyday, I'd just have my compressor ready to fill them.

So why are they worth pumping up every day? They're light. I've read poly tubes are even lighter. I put them in a pair of GP5000 and they really roll. They're also reported to have low rolling resistance, maybe a couple watts lower than butyl. No flats after a couple hundred miles, even a few miles of gravel. If they keep going like this, I might stick with them over butyl -- and I just do recreational touring -- hey, why pump harder than you have to? It adds up over the long haul.

Update: The front tube developed a leak at about 250 miles. There is a small crack about half a millimeter on the latex on the inner circumference of the tube. This would be against the Velox Fond de Jante rim tape, so not a puncture and not a pinch flat either. It would seem this latex is not that durable. I can patch it with another piece of latex and glue, but until I get around to it, I've put in a butyl tube -- all the LBS had in stock.
text_fidelity_b: Vittoria Competition Latex Tube - Performance Bike Tire Tube - Lightweight Bicycle Inner Tubes for Racing

text_fidelity_a:
Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large [[VIDEOID:3a1d0e8884973fd7767817b61417e9f7]] I've been snorkeling a few places around the world and I've learned just enough to know that good gear and good locations make all the difference.

I've had the chance to try out the Seaview 180 snorkeling mask from Wildhorn Outfitters. The Seaview 180 is different type of snorkel mask. The mask fits around your entire face - covering your eyes, nose and mouth.

I've experienced snorkeling in the Gulf of Mexico, off a deserted island in south america, in Belize, Thailand, and Nicaragua and Costa Rica. I felt like I wanted my own gear that fits and works right every time - so I finally ordered Wildhorn Outfitters Seaview 180 after having kept an eye on it for a while.

Over the last few months I've tried out a few products from Wildhorn outfitters and I've walked away impressed every time. This time was no different.

After trying this mask I had one big regret - not ordering this mask a few months ago. I really wish I could have used it last month in Central America but I know I will definitely be bringing it on my trip to Belize next year. Here's why:

Pros:

Visibility - It's hard to describe how amazing the visibility is in this mask. It is a completely different experience than any other snorkel equipment that I have ever used.

Breathing - With this mask the breathing experience is totally different. I'm not worried about breathing at all - which is kind of weird. When snorkeling I usually have to think about how I breathe - through my mouth and not my nose - keeping a tight seal around the mouthpiece - making sure not to breathe in too late after going under the water... you get the idea. With this mask I felt so much more comfortable and normal. Because the mask covers your entire face you can breathe out of mouth or nose. Also, if you try to breathe in when submerged no water actually enters your mask. You feel the pull of trying to breathe in without air but that's it. Also, if you get water in your mask the water will drain out the bottom of the mask when you lift your head out of the water.

Fog - When I tried the mask on at my house it fogged up a little but when I actually got in the water I had no issues with fog. I was planning on purchasing some anti-fog spray but now I think I'll delay that purchase and see if I actually need it in the future.

Go Pro Mount - I've used wrist mounts and other types of chest, head, and handheld mounts with a GoPro before and none of them really capture the footage how I want when snorkeling. I often spend too much time adjusting the head mount to make sure it's filming what I want it to film. With this setup I can set it up just how I want it and not worry about it being in the way or not being aimed the right way. Adjustment is also quick and easy.

Ease of use - This is the easiest snorkel mask I've ever used. It is a little shocking how quickly I got used to it. My young daughters would absolutely love masks of their own.

Cons:

Facial hair - You do need to be aware of how much facial hair you have when using this mask. Sometimes when I travel abroad I don't bother to bring a razor but with this mask I would probably bring one. Since the mask covers your entire nose and mouth it works better when I have recently shaved.

Overall:
If you snorkel regularly or are thinking of picking up equipment for your first snorkel adventure I can't recommend this mask more highly. I can't wait to use my mask again.
text_fidelity_b: Seaview 180 Degree Panoramic Snorkel Mask- Full Face Design,Panoramic Teal,Large/Extra Large

text_fidelity_a:
Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce I really hate being the first and only 4 star review but here goes..

I got mine from RawReform, whom I dearly love, and was pleased to get it very quickly and loved all the goodies that came with it.
I HIGHLY recommend that you watch the DVD on the immune system that came with it - very interesting and well done informationally. Mine also came with a book, "Rebounding For Better Health" which I also recommend reading. This book enlightened me and I learned so much from just reading this very simple book!
I'm also glad I did as I learned the importance of 'bouncing' before you 'jump'; and what great benefit the 'health bounce' has for your body!

I completely concur with the other reviewers on the quality of the Needak and would never advise buying BELOW this quality standard. I have not tried folding it yet, so I cannot comment on the ease of doing so. (Unfolding was easy.)

(I had an entire review written and almost completed when my computer fritzed, so I'm trying to remember all the points I had previously written.)

There were a few reviews in particular that cinched the deal and 'sold' me on getting mine. I had recently been troubled with hip problems that a Chiropractor had made MUCH worse (not ALL chiros, just this one) and was getting concerned about my hip/knee pain. My normal forms of exercise were also making it worse and so I wanted to see how rebounding would help.
Let me tell you that with just a couple minutes here and a couple minutes there of doing the 'health bounce' alone has made remarkable differences in my hip/knee pain (almost gone); noticeable improvements in the 'elimination' area; and giving me deeper, restful sleep and less irritability. AND, I've even noticed a slimmer tummy!
Now, how can this be??!!! I'm only doing a COUPLE minutes here and there!
Yet, the book and the DVD will explain how this form of body movement affects your body at the deepest level - the CELLULAR level!
With that information - with those results - how is it that people aren't STAMPEDING and buying these things faster than Amazon can sell their KINDLES!!??
I think it's just a matter of time, and they will.
I realized I had been in the 'dark' too long to not have known the incredible benefits that rebounding/bouncing does for your health, but not any more!

Now..why the four stars instead of five? Well, four is still good. Even three is good. Because, although it says Soft Bounce, it was harder than I imagined. At this time, bouncing with both feet is uncomfortable for ME. My legs throb and ache. So, I've gotten around that by doing a sort of dance 'Twist'; some Jumping Jack type moves and hops and that seems to do the trick. Am I just more out of shape than I thought? Will it eventually improve? I don't know. I'll let you know.
I can't help but wish that I were able to COMPARE my rebounders bounce/feel with other rebounders of EQUAL or GREATER value in order to see if another would've been more comfortable for me, but I'll not ever have that opportunity to do so; and this was my price range and I am content with it and would recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Needak Rebounder Platinum Edition Half Fold Soft Bounce

Saris Bike Racks, Bones Car Trunk Bicycle Rack Carrier, Mounts 3 Bikes, Black The Saris Super Bones 3 is a really fantastic high end bike rack. I've been using racks by Allen for several years, and while they have their issues, I thought they were a good value. This Saris model costs 8x what my Allen rack did. The difference in price and quality is quite staggering. I can't tell you if it's worth $400, but you do get what you pay for.

The most striking difference is the stability of the Saris rack. It doesn't have lots of loose straps to fly around, and the design makes it stay solid at highway speeds. It's very easy to adjust to each trunk. I can load it up with 3 bikes and it feels secure, even at 80mph. I could not say the same for my Allen rack. The Saris is also well padded to prevent scratches to the car. It also keeps the bike pedals far away enough so they don't damage the car. With the Allen rack, my pedals totally scratched up the Civic's bumper.

The disadvantages of the Saris rack are:
- The much higher cost
- Does not fold flat for storage
- Fits less cars, such as hatchbacks

This is clearly for the serious biker, so would use it very frequently to justify the price. You know who you are.
text_fidelity_b: Saris Bike Racks, Bones Car Trunk Bicycle Rack Carrier, Mounts 3 Bikes, Black

text_fidelity_a:
MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set I have owned this 2-DVD set for several weeks now, and I am still on the fence about it. I researched it thoroughly before I purchased it, and the overall reviews seemed very positive. I am a daily exerciser and also a yoga instructor, but as I get older (I'm 49 now), I definitely have increasing aches and pains, and I know there are times when my lack of flexibility limits my yoga practice. I was hoping that Mark Lauren's Mobility Rx set would benefit me in these areas.

I will first provide a brief overview of the workouts, then detail what I liked/didn't like. Both DVDs have a Main Menu which includes selection for Introduction (Lauren's 2-minute explanation of these workouts, which you can find on YouTube), Warm Up (the same for both workouts, and Workout (1 or 2). There is also an option for Music on/off and Closed Captioning on/off.

The Warm-up is what Lauren calls a "movement prep," and it clocks in at 9:39 minutes. In has nice, full-body joint mobility work such as windshield wiper knees, hydrant hip rotations, trunk rotations, one leg bridges, lunges with torso twist, squat, and lunges with lateral reach. Workout #1 is 34 minutes total, including a 4 1/2 minute description of each of the four exercises. (Note that it is NOT easy to skip this. You can select the workout from the Main Menu without doing the Warm-up, but it is also NOT easy to return to the Main Menu AFTER doing the Warm-up for some reason.) There are three rounds in this workout, and they clock in at 8:53, 9:22, and 11:12. The exercises are side-lying snow angel, isometric lunge, zombie squat, and scorpion complex, and they get progressively more challenging with each round. Workout #2 has the same structure but with different exercises. This workout is shorter, with 3 1/2 minute introduction and three rounds of 7:24, 7:37, and 8:14 to clock at 27 minutes total. The exercises are seated roll, straddle reach, spider crawl, and gate swing complex. All of the exercises are well-described in other reviews for those wanting more details.

What I like about Mobility Rx is much shorter than what I don't like, so I will start with that.

WHAT I LIKED ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The exercises themselves. For the most part, these felt like functional fitness movements that definitely have the potential to benefit my body.
*The Warm-up. Although almost 10 minutes is long for a warm-up, this would make a nice little stand-alone stretch routine; it could also work as a cool-down after other activity.

Okay, that's about all I can think of, so on to what I didn't like.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The fact that they are on 2 separate DVDs. This may seem minor, but there's only a little over an hour of content, so making this set 2 separate DVDs not only feels wasteful to me but also feels like a marketing gimmick, as if they are trying to deceive customers.
*The very poor production values. Honestly, I often don't even notice these types of things on workout DVDs (and I have literally tried 100s), but there were MULTIPLE issues here, including the following: 1) the music - it was just bad, loud and on a repetitive loop (although at least there was a music off option), 2) the sound - it was out of sync with the screen, which is VERY annoying if you are actually looking at Lauren while doing the workout, 3) the menus - as mentioned above, options such as skipping forward and returning to the Main Menu did not work correctly, and 4) the set - also just awful, with a frame around the screen that appears as if you are looking into a 1980s computer and empty fake wood boxes stacked in the corner for no reason
*Lauren's instruction. Other than telling viewers to stand or sit with "tall PRETTY posture"--an awful expression that he uses over and over--he provides little instruction on form and absolutely no modifications. The initial preview of the exercises for each workout offers an anatomical view of the muscles being worked, but Lauren never refers back to this during the workouts themselves, never connecting the movements with the actual benefits for the body.
*The disparity between the two workouts. As you can see by my description above, the first workout is significant longer than the second, but it is also MUCH harder. The second exercise, the isometric lunge, is actually a lunge with the shin placed vertical against a wall/other structure. I would consider this an advanced movement--I have done it in yoga classes only after significantly more prep work than Lauren provides here. Similarly, the fourth exercise, scorpion complex, also incorporate yoga-type movements (plank and downward facing dog), and it requires a good deal of stamina and endurance.

In summary, I believe that these routines are appropriate ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED EXERCISERS. Although I definitely fall into that category myself, and I do see some utility to the movements Lauren offers here, the downsides of this set are a significant detraction for me, and I have not yet decided whether or not I will keep it.
text_fidelity_b: MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker Well.  I have been using this for many months.  I waited to be provide a fair and honest assessment. This is a review of my personal experience.  My main disappointment is the syncing with the fitbit app - I have a samsung android smart phone with the app installed, further - the app is current with all provided updates. The fitbit 3 itself needs to be "restarted" multiple times a week- you must attach it to the charging cable, push/hold the side button and hold for up to 10 seconds to force restart.  Otherwise it does NOT sync.  SUPER annoying.  And then there are the times when it randomly decides NOT to record my sleep record.  GRRRR....  I have had multiple fitbits - beginning with their gen one version.  Provides reasonably accurate info - BUT if you must FIGHT to get the info through sync - it sort of looses it appeal.  While it says that it does allow you to swim, so water friendly, I do not soak or submerge the fitbit.  I don't remove it as I wash dishes or my hands - so it has been splashed with water.  When I get in the pool, I take it off.  I just don't trust the water friendly part.  I may go back to my fitbit 2 because it is so much more slim and attractive.  These are somewhat clunky.  I also have tried the much larger watch face version - I quickly stopped using it as it is horribly uncomfortable in size alone - the fitbit 3 is much better than that watch face/square version.  The bands on the fitbit 3 are easy to change.  I have not placed a screen/face protection shields on and haven't had too much trouble with scratching - in fact I don't see any - yet.  So I can't say how easy it is to replace the face - or to place the protection screening on.  I wear my fitbit on one wrist during the day and change it to the other wrist at night while sleeping - I use an alcohol wipe to clean the back of the unit and band several times a week. Further I don't wear it one or two nights a week to give my skin a break and to charge it.  I did purchase the perforated (holes in the band) to provide more breathability.  It is a workable step monitor.  I just wish it would sync more reliably and without forcing a restart which you can't just do where ever you are - but must be done while attached to the charging cord.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful and I hope this info was helpful to you in some way.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker
